newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle crew tackle problem power generator.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle crew tackle problem power generator.

text.p: The crew of the space shuttle Columbia was troubleshooting a malfunctioning power generator on Saturday as they opened their space laboratory for business.
One of Columbia's three crucial electricity-generating fuel cells was behaving unusually, mission commentator Steve Nesbitt said.
"One of the interior segments of that fuel cell is showing some small indications of degradation," he said.

NASA officials said they were uncertain how serious the problem was, which affected about a third of the fuel cell's electricity-generating capacity. They hoped that purging the device with water would flush out any contamination that might be causing the malfunctions.

The shuttle can operate on one fuel cell, but safety rules require an early end to the mission if any of the three onboard fail. Without electrical power the shuttle would be crippled and unable to return to Earth.
The fuel cell exhibited unusual voltage readings during the final hours of the countdown but then returned to normal.
While mission commander Jim Halsell and pilot Susan Still tried to fix the generator, astronauts Donald Thomas and Greg Linteris set up experiments in the shuttle's laboratory.
The astronauts, who blasted off from Florida on Friday, were to spend 16 days in space working on 33 major experiments.
They will light dozens of controlled fires to study the behaviour of flames in space and grow protein crystals that NASA hopes will help the fight against cancer, diabetes, AIDS and other ailments.
The shuttle was due back on Earth on April 20.
